title: Priestly Service
summary: These passages show priestly service in several settings: Exodus and Leviticus give festival instructions, 1 Kings narrates the temple dedication, and Hebrews argues that repeated offerings cannot bring the completion it attributes to Jesus' offering. The passages do different work; a calendar of worship, a temple dedication, and Hebrews' theological argument should not be read as one continuous description of ritual practice.
historical_context: Exodus 23 and Leviticus 23 set out recurring festivals, including the Feast of Unleavened Bread. In 1 Kings 8, priests carry the ark into the temple during Solomon's dedication, and a cloud fills the house. Hebrews 10 interprets sacrificial repetition through its argument about Jesus' offering and quotes the promise of a new covenant. These texts illuminate particular instructions, a narrative event, and a later biblical interpretation; they do not by themselves establish an uninterrupted history of priestly practice or describe Second Temple worship in detail.
literary_context: Exodus 23 and Leviticus 23 give festival legislation; 1 Kings 8 tells a temple-dedication story; Hebrews 10 develops an argument about sacrifice and cites Jeremiah's new-covenant promise. The literary form changes from instructions to narrative to theological argument. Hebrews' conclusion belongs to its own argument and should not be presented as a neutral description of how every worshiper understood the earlier rites.
covenantal_significance: The festival instructions order recurring worship, while the dedication scene links the temple with prayer for Israel and for foreigners who seek God there. Hebrews then argues that Jesus' offering accomplishes what repeated offerings could not and connects this claim with the new-covenant promise. Each passage makes its own connection between worship and covenant life.
canonical_role: Together, the references let readers compare Israel's festival calendar, a royal account of temple dedication, and Hebrews' interpretation of sacrifice. This provides a focused way to trace priestly-service language across biblical texts while keeping their settings and claims distinct.

interpretive_notes.note: Exodus 23:14-17 and Leviticus 23:1-8 describe recurring festivals; 1 Kings 8 narrates the priests carrying the ark into the newly dedicated temple. These are different kinds of evidence about worship, not one ritual repeated in every setting.

Hebrews 10:1-18 argues that repeated offerings cannot bring the completion it associates with Jesus' offering and cites the new-covenant promise. This is Hebrews' theological reading of sacrifice, not a complete history of Israelite worship practice.
